subject: general
question: What is the function of subsidiary cells?

options.text: Support of guard cells in stomatal function
Secretion of enzymes for nutrient acquisition, defence and digestion

solution:
The correct answer is __**Support of guard cells in stomatal function**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Subsidiary cells are specialized epidermal cells that are associated with guard cells and help in stomatal function.
 
• They play an indirect role in regulating the opening and closing of stomata by providing mechanical support to guard cells.
 
• Subsidiary cells contribute to maintaining the ion balance and turgor pressure required for guard cells to function effectively.
 
• These cells are part of the stomatal complex, which is crucial for gas exchange and transpiration in plants.
 
• The presence of subsidiary cells varies among plant species and is a characteristic feature used for plant identification.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Stomata:**

 
 
• Stomata are microscopic pores present on the surface of leaves and stems that facilitate gas exchange (CO2 intake and O2 release).
 
• They are surrounded by guard cells, which regulate their opening and closing based on environmental conditions.
 
 
 
• **Guard Cells:**
 
 
• Guard cells are specialized cells that control the size of the stomatal pore by changing their shape.
 
• They respond to factors like light, water availability, and internal CO2 concentration.
 
 
 
• **Subsidiary Cells:**
 
 
• Subsidiary cells are part of the epidermis and surround guard cells, forming the stomatal complex.
 
• They vary in shape, size, and arrangement depending on the plant species.
 
 
 
• **Function of Stomatal Complex:**
 
 
• Facilitates transpiration and cooling of the plant.
 
• Plays a key role in photosynthesis by enabling CO2 uptake.
 
• Helps maintain the plant's water balance by regulating water loss.
